memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Every tithe of the herd and flock - every tenth animal that passes
under the shepherd's rod - will be holy to the LORD. No one may pick out
the good from the bad or make any substitution. If anyone does make a
substitution, both the animal and its substitute become holy and cannot
be redeemed'" - Lev 27:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture the scene. The shepherd's animals pass one by one under his rod,
and every tenth one is set apart for the Lord. There was no picking and
choosing — no keeping the healthy animals for yourself and giving God the
weak tenth. Whatever the tenth one happened to be, that was God's.

This removed all calculation and self-interest. The person could not
manipulate the outcome to give God his worst. He simply counted honestly
and gave whatever fell to the Lord's portion.

Dear friend, there is deep honesty required here. It is a picture of
giving God our genuine share rather than our carefully selected leftovers.
How often do we give God the time, energy or resources that happen to be
left after we have taken the best for ourselves?

There is also a tender image hidden in this verse. The Lord Himself is
described as our shepherd, and we pass under His watchful care. The
psalmist says we are the sheep of His pasture (Ps 100:3). Jesus said, I am
the good shepherd; the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep
(John 10:11).

The shepherd's rod that counted the sheep also guarded and guided them.
As you consider what you give God, remember that you yourself are counted,
known and kept by the Shepherd who gave His life for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I give God my genuine share or my carefully chosen leftovers?
2. Where am I tempted to calculate my giving to my own advantage?
3. What comfort do I find in being counted and kept by the Good Shepherd?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me give You my honest share rather than my leftovers. Thank
You that I am counted, known and kept by the Good Shepherd who laid down
His life for me. Amen.
